sections.html:
Orchard Park is a town with a village inside it. The town covers 38.52 square miles about 14 miles southeast of downtown Buffalo, so the first question is whether your lot lies in the village or out in the town. The area broke from Hamburg in 1850, was named Ellicott and then East Hamburgh, and became Orchard Park on March 1, 1934.

Hamlets within the town limits include Armor, Duells Corner, Ellicott, Loveland and Webster Corners. Highmark Stadium stands in the hamlet of Windom at the town's western edge, while Chestnut Ridge Park, the largest park in Erie County, anchors the south. US 219 follows the west side, US 20 across the north, and NY 277 and NY 240 meet near US 20.

Showings turn to schools quickly. Orchard Park Central School District has four K-5 buildings (Eggert, Ellicott, South Davis and Windom), one middle school and one high school. Put the correct elementary school in your listing and buyers have one less thing to ask.

The town had 29,804 residents in mid-2025, living in 12,829 households. Homeowners live in 74.5 percent of the housing, the typical owned home is valued at $360,700, and median rent is $1,304 a month. Monthly owner costs have a median of $2,323 with a mortgage and $910 without.

Households rarely move: 91.6 percent of residents were at the same address a year earlier. With few houses changing hands, a well-prepared one gets noticed, so tidy presentation and clean paperwork count.

sections.h2: Which Orchard Park offices handle permits, assessments and recording?
sections.html:
Four offices touch almost every part of a sale.

  • Assessor's Office: keeps your assessment, takes informal review requests and receives grievance paperwork. Phone 716-662-6420.
  • Building Inspector and Code Enforcement: permits, inspections and zoning verification letters, from the Municipal Center on South Buffalo Street in the village. Weekday lunch closure at the counter runs 1 PM to 2 PM.
  • Town Board: holds meetings in the Municipal Building courtroom on the first and third Wednesdays monthly.
  • Erie County Clerk: files the deed and takes in the transfer tax.

The town has been reviewing rezoning near the stadium along with zoning map amendments. Own a parcel by the stadium or on a corridor under study? Ask the building office for a zoning verification letter before pricing the house.

You can contest an assessment only in the spring, around Grievance Day on the fourth Tuesday of May. The Assessor's Office works from the calendar below and reports a 1990 revaluation, a uniform level of assessment of 28.5 percent and 12,412 parcels.

Orchard Park assessment calendar
Assessment stepOrchard Park date
Taxable status dateMarch 1
Valuation dateJuly 1 of the previous year
Tentative rollMay 1
Grievance DayFourth Tuesday of May
Final rollJuly 1

At 28.5 percent, the assessed value printed on your notice is well under market value, so it is not a price. Hearing requests are due before Grievance Day. Hearings run from 4 PM to 8 PM in the Town Hall basement meeting room, and email or upload submissions are not accepted. Bring Form RP-524 and supporting documents, with copies for each of the five review board members. Phone the assessor for this year's schedule, and read the assessment review page first.

Village houses may have a second assessment, since villages that assess property accept their own RP-524 complaints. Ask whether yours is one.

Sellers here pay one combined transfer tax: $4.50 for each $500 of price, with any leftover fraction rounded up to a full $500. New York gets $2.00 and Erie County gets $2.50, collected by the clerk as the deed is filed. A seller who is 62 or older and has lived in a one or two family home for at least a year can sign an affidavit, free at the clerk's office, to pay only $2.00 per $500.

Recording is billed separately. On the clerk's residential deed schedule the statutory fee is $45, every written side of a page adds $5, Form TP-584 is $10 and the RP-5217 transfer report is $125, which puts a three-page deed at $195. A 1 percent mansion tax applies from $1 million up, paid by the buyer.

sections.h2: Paperwork that can slow a closing
sections.html:
Start with the state's seller questionnaire. Real Property Law 462 has the owner of a house with up to four units sign it and deliver it ahead of the buyer's signature on the contract. An as-is clause is still allowed. Several questions line up with local houses:

  • Are there certificates of occupancy for the building?
  • Is the water municipal or from a well, and does waste go to a public sewer or a septic tank?
  • Has the lot had flooding, drainage trouble or water in the structure?
  • What school district is the address in?

Starting work before the permit is issued means paying a double fee. The permit list includes decks, fences, sheds, pools, roofing, furnace and air conditioning replacements, generators and added plumbing fixtures, and the town has asked for plumbing permits on all plumbing work since January 2020. Owners must also clear snow and ice from sidewalks beside their land. Close out or disclose any gap before an inspector or buyer spots it.

sections.h2: When does a cash purchase suit an Orchard Park owner?
sections.html:
No lender means no appraisal or loan approval to wait on, leaving title work, state forms and recording. Cash appeals to owners who want to avoid showings and repairs, such as heirs to a house or people moving on a set date.

On any route, start by collecting your tax bill, permit records for earlier work and the Erie County deed details. Keep offers in writing, decide who pays each closing cost, and have a New York attorney review the contract before signing. Expect the disclosure form, the transfer tax and any lien payoff to land on you as seller. Ask the title company for a payoff letter from any lender so the figure is ready when the closing date is set.

A simple order of work helps. First, check with the building office for open permits. Second, read the seller questionnaire and answer it. Third, ask the Assessor's Office whether your house is in the village or the town, since that decides which assessment applies. Fourth, line up an attorney. Doing these before you accept an offer keeps the closing from stalling on small items, and a cash buyer with a fixed date will expect them done.

faqs.q: Does the buyer or the seller cover Orchard Park's transfer tax?
faqs.a: The seller pays. Erie County's combined rate is $4.50 per $500, made up of $2.00 for the state and $2.50 for the county. A qualifying seller aged 62 or older may pay the reduced $2.00 rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell an Orchard Park house that needs repairs?
faqs.a: Yes, because both sides may agree to sell as-is. The signed seller questionnaire still goes to the buyer first, so answer honestly from what you know.

faqs.q: When is Grievance Day in Orchard Park?
faqs.a: It is the fourth Tuesday of May. The Assessor's Office can confirm the exact date, the appointment deadline and how many copies of the complaint form to bring.

faqs.q: What should I do about unpermitted work on my Orchard Park house?
faqs.a: Talk to the building office before listing. A late permit costs a double fee, and the state questionnaire asks about certificates of occupancy. Resolving it now beats renegotiating a contract later.

faqs.q: Which office records an Orchard Park deed?
faqs.a: The Erie County Clerk, who also collects the transfer tax at the same visit. A three-page residential deed costs $195 to record. Your attorney or title company usually files it.
